newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Howard rejects Colston support.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Howard rejects Colston support.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Wednesday the government would no longer accept the support of key independent Mal Colston, accused of abusing travel expenses, if he remained in the upper house of parliament.
"We won't accept his vote in the future," Howard told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.

"And the way that we will not accept his vote is to arrange that if he does decide to support the government on an issue we will arrange for one of our number to drop out of the division (vote) so that his vote is not in effect counted."
Colston's vote has been crucial to the government passing key reforms, including budget cuts, through the Senate, where it does not have a majority.
Howard said his cabinet of senior ministers made the decision after detailed consideration of the Colston affair during its regular meeting on Tuesday.
"I am making it clear this morning that in all of the circumstances if Senator Colston remains a member of the Senate we will not in future accept his vote," Howard said.
Howard stopped short of specifically demanding Colston quit the Senate, a move urged by the Labor opposition and the Australian Democrats, the third power bloc in the Senate.
The government last week called on Colston, under police investigation over corruption allegations, to step down from the influential post of Senate deputy president.
Colston, who is in a Brisbane hospital suffering from a lung infection, denies any illegal activity and has refused to take any action until he recovers.
The government, Labor and the Democrats have all said they would dump Colston from the deputy presidency if he did not step aside voluntarily by the time the Senate resumes on May 6.
